notes.meaning: Before anything was made, the Word was already there. The Word is the Son of God, who shares God's thoughts and heart with the world. He was together with God the Father from eternity, and He was truly God.
Jesus existed with God the Father before time began. He is a distinct person from the Father, yet completely united with Him in nature. Nothing about His divine life ever had a starting point.
The Word created the entire universe. Every single thing, from the largest star to the smallest bug, was made through Him. Nothing exists that He did not bring into being.
The Word is the overflowing fountain of all life. He gives physical breath to living creatures and gives spiritual light to human minds. His truth brings wisdom, holiness, and joy to our hearts.

The light of Christ keeps shining brightly in this dark, sinful world. People caught in spiritual darkness tried to resist and put out the light, but they could never defeat it. God's truth continues to shine without fading.
God sent a prophet named John the Baptist on a special mission. He was an ordinary man with an extraordinary task given by heaven. His job was to prepare people to meet the coming Savior.
John arrived to tell people the truth about the Light. He came to point everyone toward Jesus so that all who heard might believe. His whole ministry was meant to build faith in Christ.
John the Baptist was not the promised Light himself. He was only a witness who spoke about the Light. His duty was to guide people's eyes away from himself and onto Jesus.
Jesus is the true and perfect Light coming into the world. He gives light to every person through human reason and conscience. He alone guides lost people safely to God.

differ.view: This light reaches every person as conscience, a sense of right and wrong. It is graciously given by Christ to show people their sin, and if people did not resist it, it would grow brighter and brighter.
This verse speaks only of the common light of reason and conscience that all people have. It is not saving grace offered equally to everyone. Only God's Spirit opens heaven to those he has chosen.

notes.meaning: The Word entered the very world He had created. Even though He formed the earth and everything in it, the people of the world did not recognize their Maker. Their sin blinded them to His presence.
Jesus came to His own homeland and visited His own chosen people, the Jews. Sadly, the nation as a whole refused to welcome Him or believe His message. They turned away from their promised King.

A faithful few did welcome Jesus and put their trust in Him. To everyone who believes in Him, He gives the wonderful right to become children of God. God adopts all who trust in Christ into His heavenly family.

differ.view: No one can believe unless God has first given them new birth. Faith itself flows from this new birth, and it is God's gift from heaven.
The moment people believe, they become God's children. Then God sends the Spirit of his Son into their hearts, so they cry out, "Father."

notes.meaning: Becoming a child of God does not come from family background, human effort, or physical birth. Nobody can inherit salvation through earthly parents. This new life is a spiritual rebirth that comes entirely from God.

notes.meaning: The eternal Word became a real human being and lived among us on earth. His followers saw His divine glory displayed through His miracles, character, and love. He was full of God's unfailing grace and perfect truth.

John the Baptist spoke out boldly and told the crowds the truth about Jesus. He explained that Jesus was greater than him in honor and rank, because Jesus existed long before him in eternity. John wanted everyone to see Christ's supreme importance.

All believers draw spiritual strength and goodness out of the rich fullness of Jesus. He gives His people endless blessings, pouring out one gift of grace after another. There is always more grace available in Christ than we could ever use.

God gave the holy law through Moses to teach people right from wrong and show them their need for help. But the full gifts of forgiveness, grace, and eternal truth came through Jesus Christ. The law showed our guilt, while Jesus brought our rescue.

No human being has ever seen the full essence of God with physical eyes. But Jesus, God's only Son, enjoys the closest possible relationship with the Father. Because Jesus is God, He alone explains God fully to us.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Older translations say "the only begotten Son" here. Robertson says the best old manuscripts read "God only begotten" instead, which is the basis for the BSB's "who is Himself God."

notes.meaning: The Jewish rulers in Jerusalem sent a group of priests and temple assistants to question John. John's powerful preaching had drawn huge crowds, so the leaders wanted an official explanation of his work. They asked him directly who he was.
John did not hide anything or pretend to be someone he was not. He plainly and openly told the messengers that he was not the Messiah. He refused to take any honor that belonged only to Jesus.

The leaders then asked John if he was the prophet Elijah returned from heaven, or the special prophet Moses had promised. John told them clearly that he was neither of those men in person. He kept turning their attention away from popular rumors.

The messengers pressed John for a clear answer so they could report back to the high council in Jerusalem. They had to know what title or mission he claimed for himself. They wanted his own words about his identity.

John answered by quoting the prophet Isaiah from the Old Testament. He described himself merely as a voice shouting out in the lonely wilderness, telling people to smooth out a straight road for the Lord. He wanted people to clear away their sins to welcome the King.

The men sent on this assignment belonged to the Pharisees, a strict religious party devoted to Jewish laws and traditions. They guarded religious customs very carefully and watched out for new teachers. Their strict standards explain why they challenged John.

The Pharisees asked why John was baptizing people if he was not the Messiah, Elijah, or the Prophet. Washing in water was normally used when non-Jews joined the faith, not for Jewish people. They wondered who gave John the authority to introduce this practice.

John explained that he only baptized with water to call people to turn from sin. He revealed that the great Messiah was already standing among the crowd, even though the people did not recognize Him. The long-awaited Savior was already right in their midst.
